waves.name: The MAINJOB chain
waves.rationale: The only entry point in the tree is job:MAINJOB, and its single step runs PGMMAIN, which calls PGMLIVE. That is the whole reachable system. The family is sound: the job opens no dataset, so there is nothing shared to sequence around, no rollback that has to unwind a data change, and the boundary to assert equivalence at is the job's return code and SYSOUT. It is a valid wave by all four tests, but it is valid the way a single-brick wall is structurally sound: there is nothing else it could have been. The real caveat is that a one-step job running two no-op programs cannot be the nightly batch cycle the client named as must-not-break, so treat this plan as covering the fragment on disk, not the cycle.
waves.unblocks: Nothing inside this tree, because there is no wave 2. Outside it, this wave is worth running only as a toolchain proof: it establishes the build, deploy, flag and rollback path for COBOL batch on the target runtime against a unit with zero blast radius, before the real nightly cycle arrives.
